Q: Getting delta between two dates of different timezones A:

The issue is how you are localizing the date there is a Z on the end meaning its UTC but you are using localize() and adding CET on it which just stamps a timezone without shifting the time.

In a way you are saying "Its CET" but its not, its UTC.

Here is a solution

First I created file.json to import dt

{
    "dt": "2026-02-27T19:30:00Z"
}

Then

import datetime
import pytz
import json


with open("file.json", "r") as f:
    jsonfile = json.load(f)

cet = pytz.timezone("Europe/Berlin")
utc = pytz.utc


dateJson = datetime.datetime.strptime(jsonfile["dt"], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
dateJson = utc.localize(dateJson)
dateJson = dateJson.astimezone(cet)

dateNow = datetime.datetime.now(tz=cet)


timeDelta = dateJson - dateNow
print(timeDelta)

Q: javax.servlet.ServletException: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space A:

Since you mentioned that you still have problem even if you increase the heap memory to 2gb, it is clear that you have memory leak in your code. Unused objects are not dereferenced so that they would be removed by the Garbage collector.

Using more heap memory than actually required would have performance impact. Over provisioning of heap memory does not solve the issue in your case. Instead it would have poor performance (lengthy pause time). You need to profile your code using any profiler (Java Mission Control, Java Visual VM, Your Kit java profiler, etc.) to see which object takes more memory space in heap. If you can share your code, then we will be able to find where exactly the memory leak occurs.
